lead.headline: Anthropic Prices a Record $81 Billion IPO Above Range as Hawkish Fed Minutes Rattle Wall Street
lead.deck: The Claude maker sold upsized stock at $83 a share, valuing it near $1.5 trillion ahead of its Nasdaq debut today, while minutes from the Fed's October meeting pushed the S&P 500 to a fifth straight loss.
body: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, above the $70–78 range it had marketed, and enlarged the deal to about 980 million shares from 825 million. The sale raises roughly $81.3 billion, overtaking SpaceX's June listing as the largest IPO on record by gross proceeds, and gives the company a fully diluted value of about $1.5 trillion. The shares are due to begin trading on Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT.

Alongside the offering, a group of technology companies including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD agreed to buy a combined $26 billion of stock at the IPO price. The prospectus shows revenue of $33.24 billion for the nine months to September, up roughly twelvefold, and an annualised revenue run rate of about $81 billion at the end of October. Each of the seven co-founders is selling 3.38 million shares. Amazon, which holds a large stake, rose 3.8%.

The listing landed on a difficult day for the broader market. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed almost all officials expect further rate rises may be needed, and a few argued for a half-point move if inflation data came in hot. The S&P 500 gave up early gains to close 0.23% lower at 7,323.64, slipping below its 200-day moving average, and the Dow fell 1.11%. The Nasdaq rose 0.42% as AMD and Amazon gained.

Nvidia fell 2.9% the day after beating forecasts, as uncertainty over Jensen Huang's exit lingered. The dollar climbed to a 19-month high, gold slid 3.5% to about $3,729 an ounce and markets now price a near-certain quarter-point Fed increase in December.

top: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, above range, raising about $81.3 billion in the largest listing on record; trading starts today.
Fed minutes showed nearly all officials see more hikes ahead, sending the S&P 500 to a fifth straight loss and the dollar to a 19-month high.
Health insurers plunged as Humana fell 13% and UnitedHealth 10% on a plan to widen Medicare Advantage audits.
Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy AI start-up Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock, and its shares jumped about 10%.
Indian shares snapped a two-day rally on profit booking, with Titan down 5% as gold and silver slid.

items.headline: Fed Minutes Flip Wall Street Into the Red
items.body: The S&P 500 was higher until the October minutes showed broad support for further tightening, then closed lower for a fifth day, its longest losing run since June. Health care dragged while tech and consumer names held up.

items.headline: Asia Rebounds on Nvidia, Europe Slides
items.body: The Kospi reclaimed 5,000 as SK Hynix rallied on Nvidia's results and the Nikkei snapped a four-day losing streak. European indices fell for a second day, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng lost 0.91%.

items.headline: Profit Booking Pulls Indian Shares Off Nine-Month Highs
items.body: Benchmarks fell after a roughly 13% rally over 12 sessions, with metal, auto and IT stocks leading losses and declining shares outnumbering gainers about two to one. PSU banks, pharma and media edged higher.

items.headline: Dollar Hits 19-Month High as Gold Sinks
items.body: Gold fell 3.5% to its lowest since September 2025 and silver dropped almost 5%, while WTI crude slid 3.2% after a large US inventory build. Cheaper oil helped the rupee firm slightly to about 93.44 per dollar.

items.headline: Insurers Sink as Medicare Audit Plan Widens
items.body: A proposal from the US Medicare agency would let audit findings be applied to broader payments and recover improper payments dating back to 2018, extending the previous day's sell-off in managed-care stocks.

items.headline: Retailers Rally on Upbeat Holiday Outlooks
items.body: TJX beat on comparable sales and raised its full-year outlook, and Target gained on a positive holiday forecast. Take-Two climbed ahead of the Grand Theft Auto VI rollout; Walmart reports today.

items.headline: Cybersecurity Jumps While Nvidia Slips
items.body: Security stocks rallied on Palo Alto's results and guidance and after a US agency urged organisations to patch a critical Java flaw. Nvidia lost ground despite its beat, after its chair reiterated that Huang will not return.

items.headline: Titan Tumbles as Gold Slides; Cipla Gains on FDA Clearance
items.body: Jewellery stocks fell as gold and silver extended their slide for a sixth session. Cipla rose after the US FDA closed an inspection of its InvaGen plant with no action indicated.

items.headline: Palo Alto Buys Applied Compute for $4.5 Billion
items.body: The cybersecurity group will acquire the San Francisco AI start-up, founded by former OpenAI staff, at about $1.25 billion above its valuation from a funding round earlier this month. It follows Palo Alto's earlier deals for CyberArk and Chronosphere.

items.headline: Textron Sells Industrial Arm to Kingswood
items.body: An affiliate of Kingswood Capital Management will buy the Kautex and Specialized Vehicles businesses, leaving Textron a pure aerospace and defence company. Textron plans to use the proceeds for buybacks in 2027.

items.headline: Fairfax Exits IIFL Finance
items.body: Fairfax Financial sold its entire stake in the Indian lender through a block deal, and IIFL's shares rose about 4% on the day.

items.headline: Mufin Green Finance to Buy Into BimaPay
items.body: The listed NBFC's board approved buying a 23% stake in the insurtech start-up for ₹66 crore.

items.headline: Macro Funds Lead a Losing October
items.body: Citco data show hedge funds lost 1.2% on average in October, with global macro and equity strategies hit hardest while event-driven funds made money. Investors still added money for a tenth straight month, bringing year-to-date inflows to $136 billion.

items.headline: Coatue Set for a Windfall From Anthropic
items.body: Bloomberg reported that Coatue's holding in Anthropic was worth about $10 billion at the IPO's target valuation, which would be higher at the final $83 price.

items.headline: Activists Walk Away From Dick's Sporting Goods
items.body: Filings show four activist funds sold out of the retailer in the third quarter after a profit warning, while Browning West doubled its holding and remains the one still pressing the company.

items.fig: ₹485 cr Series E · ≈200 stores · FY26 revenue >₹1,150 cr
items.headline: Style Union Raises ₹485 Crore to Push Into North and West India
items.body: Venturi Partners and Elev8 co-led the round for the value-fashion brand, founded by Rakesh and Ekta Biyani, which competes with Zudio and V-Mart. It is one of several D2C fashion brands betting on physical stores.

items.fig: $15m Series A · 4 cr eggs a month · FY27 target >₹350 cr
items.headline: Egg Brand Henfruit Takes First Outside Money
items.body: Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures backed the brand, which had been bootstrapped for more than a decade. It plans to widen distribution beyond quick-commerce and marketplaces and leans on lab testing as food regulators step up scrutiny.

items.headline: Ribbit Trims Groww Stake; PB Fintech Co-Founder Steps Back
items.body: Ribbit Capital sold part of its Groww holding through block deals. Separately, PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal is stepping down from his executive role.

items.headline: QSR and Robotics Start-Ups Draw Capital
items.body: Bubble-tea chain Boba Bhai raised $18 million to build a multi-brand quick-service restaurant group, and Humyn Labs raised $47 million to collect training data for robots.
